description: Model lineage: each edge records what a child model kept, changed, or added from its parent.

nodes.title: Dixit 1989
nodes.citation: Dixit, A. (1989). Entry and exit decisions under uncertainty. Journal of Political Economy, 97(3), 620–638.
nodes.role: Shows that sunk costs and uncertainty make firms delay exit: they wait rather than leave on a bad signal.

nodes.title: Gimeno et al. 1997
nodes.citation: Gimeno, J., Folta, T. B., Cooper, A. C., & Woo, C. Y. (1997). Survival of the fittest? Administrative Science Quarterly, 42(4), 750–783.
nodes.role: A venture persists while performance exceeds a threshold set by the owner's alternatives. General human capital raises the threshold; venture-specific human capital lowers it.

nodes.title: Levinthal & Wu 2010
nodes.citation: Levinthal, D. A., & Wu, B. (2010). Opportunity costs and non-scale free capabilities. Strategic Management Journal, 31(7), 780–801.
nodes.role: Distinguishes resources that carry an opportunity cost across uses from those that can be shared at no cost.

nodes.title: Dixit & Pindyck 1994
nodes.citation: Dixit, A. K., & Pindyck, R. S. (1994). Investment under uncertainty. Princeton University Press.
nodes.role: Formalizes the option value of waiting, which pushes the exit point below the break-even threshold.

nodes.title: Lieberman et al. 2017
nodes.citation: Lieberman, M. B., Lee, G. K., & Folta, T. B. (2017). Entry, exit, and the potential for resource redeployment. Strategic Management Journal, 38(3), 526–544.
nodes.role: A firm exits a business when its cash flow falls below the value it could recover by redeploying the business's resources.

nodes.title: Giustiziero et al. 2023
nodes.citation: Giustiziero, G., Kretschmer, T., Somaya, D., & Wu, B. (2023). Hyperspecialization and hyperscaling. Strategic Management Journal, 44(6), 1391–1424.
nodes.role: Data and software scale at little cost, but the engineers, managers, and servers they need cannot serve two uses at once.

nodes.title: Data threshold model
nodes.citation: Working paper under review (author and title withheld for blind review).
nodes.role: A firm's survival threshold depends on how generalizable its data is. Generalizable data raises the threshold; market-specific data lowers it.

nodes.title: Feldman & Sakhartov 2022
nodes.citation: Feldman, E. R., & Sakhartov, A. V. (2022). Resource redeployment and divestiture as strategic alternatives. Organization Science, 33(3), 926–945.
nodes.role: Models how a firm exits as well as whether: redeployment dominates earlier exits and divestiture later ones. A sibling branch to be added in Stage 2.

diff.text: The threshold structure: exit when current value falls below the value of the best alternative minus switching costs
Human capital becomes a data portfolio: general vs. venture-specific human capital becomes generalizable vs. market-specific data
Portfolio size, with market-specific data defined as (1 − generalizable share) × size
Industry maturity, which lowers the alternative value of generalizable data and raises the value of specific data
The exit rule: leave when focal value falls below the value recoverable by redeploying
The alternative use need not be one of the firm's existing businesses
The value of waiting, which lets a firm stay somewhat below its threshold under uncertainty
The claim that the propositions survive unless waiting value varies enough with portfolio composition
Opportunity cost falls on the complements data needs, not on the data itself
Data is therefore treated as a non-scale-free resource in the threshold model
Exit under uncertainty and sunk costs (lineage to verify)
Economic theory of exit with sunk costs (lineage to verify)
Opportunity costs of resources across uses (lineage to verify)
Redeployment as a mode of exit (lineage to verify)
